summary.name: ATS Resume Checker
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source in-browser tool that scores a resume (0–100) against a job description, flags missing ATS keywords, and suggests fixes without uploading the file.
use_cases: Checking whether a resume parses cleanly in applicant tracking systems
Finding keywords missing from a resume compared to a job description
Getting prioritized fixes before submitting a job application
Testing a resume layout for single-column, standard-heading compatibility
Checking a text-based PDF resume privately without uploading it
summary.what_it_does: The tool scores a text-based PDF resume from 0 to 100 against a job description, checking parseable structure, standard section headings, contact details, measurable impact, and keyword overlap with the role. It flags missing ATS keywords and offers prioritized fixes. The page says the PDF is parsed locally and everything runs in the browser with JavaScript, with nothing uploaded, stored, or logged. The page also explains how ATS systems such as Workday, Greenhouse, Taleo, iCIMS and Lever parse resumes, and recommends a score of 70+ with 80+ as excellent. It advises submitting .docx for online applications and text-based PDF when emailing a recruiter.
notable: Runs entirely in the browser; resume is parsed locally and not uploaded
Open source, with a linked GitHub repo
Scores 0–100 against a specific job description and flags missing keywords
Works only with text-based PDFs, not scanned images
caveats: Accepts only text-based PDFs; scanned or image PDFs are not supported
The page promotes paid Gumroad products and an ATS Resume Kit, and the site offers an optional tip and a paid-looking checklist download; these are not part of the free tool
